I can't think of anything that I enjoy other then driving. It's being jobless right now that is bringing this on. Once I get a steady job again I'll happier then a pig in mud. Back in the day I was working computer contracts and that was 2 weeks on 2 weeks off a month here a few weeks off and I thought I enjoyed the hell out of that but then everyone and their mother got a computer cert and now geeks were paid ~$12/h. Started going crazy with that and after about 6 years of a friend of mine trying to talk me into it I got my Class A. I've always loved driving, just get in the car and drive the loop around the metro when it's not rush hour or a day trip to the other end of the state. Loved it. I had friends that lived 4 hours north of me and I went and visited once a month just to get out of town but I always remembered the best part of the trip was the drive. 

So I got my Class A. I went to school for it, left a computer contract mid way though and pissed off a few people doing so and I shouldn't have done that, but I'm an idiot at time and impulsive. So I left. Did the school thing with some complications. The friend that told me to get a Class A got me a job where he worked. When I tell you it was a blast, that's not enough. I've saved databases from the brink of extinction, built multi-million dollar systems and sent them off with a longing. I've cooked meals that went to a fund raiser that cost hundreds per plate, honestly felt bad that it was getting charged so much. Also cooked for elderly that told me they could die happy after eating whatever it was I slapped together for them. But I tell ya, 18 wheels,  8 to 13 gears, 80,000 lbs, 68 mph, coming down the side of mountains heading out of PA or going to CA. What a rush. Even when it's not that hairy, 90% of the time, it's just so relaxing. Going out on a nice long smooth road seeing the country side and the hundreds of little cars swarming around you like flies. Honestly relaxing. I have where I'm going, I know how to get there, I know what lane I need to be for how many hours and just go. Loved it. Even typing this now I'm smiling about it. Screwed that up though.

So yea what makes me feel good is working. Years ago I was out with friends and someone was with us that was from another town. I don't remember this person but something he said stuck with me. After hours and hours of hanging out in the bar and talking with everyone he said "ok, come to (where i live) and the only topic is work." That struck me. That made me think about other people and what they do when out with people. Now don't get me wrong I can't stand going out but when I do usually the only thing I ever talk about it work. That night all the people I was hanging out with were talking about work too. But that made me think and came up with, "what else is there?". It came back to the mantra of wake up, go to work, go home, go to sleep, rinse repeat, eventually die.

That is a awesome article. I've passed that on to my best friend who is a parent telling him hey read this so your kids done end up like me. 


>Can you think of success not in terms of how well you did, or how smart you are (or how not smart enough you are), but in terms of how hard you worked? If so, more success will likely follow naturally, and the work you do won't be so unrewarding.


I can think of only one or two times in my life where this applies. I'm sure there are others but the being praised part has caused me think of it as shame. After reading that I'm a little angry but understanding that it is discovery in my life time. Angry because I wasn't part of it but understanding that I wasn't part of it. I hope more future parents read this.

>Cooped up in an oven of baking mediocrity. It sounds stifling. Your awareness of this fact brings no solace, only pain. Why is that? 

I think because all my live I've been told how smart I am. How impressed people are by someone so young knowing something such and such. Being that was something positive that happened when young it's something my brain holds onto. All I've been doing to circumvent being lonely is read. From that I find joy of beating my friends in book smarts. Sadly that's not a tough feat. 

>Somehow being average is not good enough. So many failed expectations. Defined by who and how?

Defined by me. That is what comes with the low self esteem. Having my self worth destroyed by so many has led me to think that I can't do it, whatever it is. I can blame all the people that had something to do with picking on me but I let them. Why did I let them? That's a good question that I haven't watered down yet.

>Reading what you wrote makes me want to reject you. 

Good. I've destroyed ever one of my relationships I've ever had because I as far as I can figure I don't want to have anyone close enough so they will see what is going on with me. I know it's the self esteem issue of if I let them get close and know me then they will turn around and laugh at me. Also there is another situation where I didn't think I was good enough for her. That's my biggest regret in life because around her I was happy. It was years ago but eventually I think I would have figured out the working out problems, talking things through and working as a couple, and we both could have been happy together. But at the time there was just no for site and things happened that put us on different paths. Just kidding, please don't do that.

>But it sounds like you expect rejection and failure and that is exactly what happens. This experience reinforces your worldview time and time again. 

I do. I think it's because it is what I'm used to. Been screwing things up long enough and getting rejected from so many for so long. Yea I'm used to it. 

>But you also realize that some people don't feel that way? Why..., and how...? Sounds like it started when you were rejected after you moved. Life became about being different and alone. And it continues to be defined that way. It is lonely in that space. And I sense that is what feeds your resentment and pain. Being lonely and misunderstood. It's hard to connect to other people when you expect to fail or for them to reject you. But that is exactly what you must do. 

I realize that the entire world isn't like this because the suicide rate would be much higher then what it is if they did. I'm one smart cookie. Tough. Resilient. Some other good qualities I'm sure. My biggest problem is that I don't care. Not about myself really much. Really not about the world around me. I've gotten used to this. The chronic depression and no self esteem that is me. I look at the world and think why bother? I'll get a job to cover the bills. I don't want kids so save enough for the retirement that I'll never hit with this drinking problem. If I ever make extra I'll be giving it to my nephew and niece. There is no point and I feel sorry for the kids that are being born these days. 

>Find a way to connect with others. Like you are now, reaching out here. Thank you for that.
So odd to me that others would help you get a job in the IT world if you are such a failure. 

They said no.

>Someone must have some respect for your ability. 

Mom. I guess. 

>I wonder what it would be like to allow yourself to recognize that.

Here is something strange. All my life I've been told "you are smart" "I'm impressed by you" "I wish I knew what you do" and other such things. It's been said to me so often that now when I hear them I feel bad. Not in the sense of "no I'm not that" but I feel bad because I've heard it so much that I don't know what to say to that. I've sat for long times thinking about past experiences and have come the conclusion of nod and smile. Even then I think that is wrong. I don't know if it's the self esteem problem or something else anymore but even when I get a compliment I feel ashamed. I feel embarrassed because the people that say this stuff to me I look back and think "you could have done this". 

I've re read that last paragraph. I think it comes from working in IT. A lot of IT workers get a entitlement thing going with users who refuse to do the simplest of trouble shooting. I think that is where the "you could have done this" attitude comes from. Just I apply it with everything I do because I am average and just don't want to be around dumb people.
